description:
Create a spreadsheet-driven parametric L-bracket in FreeCAD. The bracket's geometry must be fully controlled by named parameters in a FreeCAD Spreadsheet object, so that changing a value in the spreadsheet automatically updates the 3D model.

**Step 1 — Create the Spreadsheet with parameters:**
Switch to the Spreadsheet workbench and create a new Spreadsheet. Define the following cells with aliases:

| Cell | Alias            | Value |
|------|------------------|-------|
| A1   | base_length      | 60    |
| A2   | base_width       | 40    |
| A3   | upright_height   | 50    |
| A4   | thickness        | 5     |

All values are in millimeters.

**Step 2 — Create the L-bracket geometry:**
Switch to the Part Design workbench. Create a Body, then create a Sketch on the XZ plane. Draw a closed L-shaped profile (angle bracket cross-section):
- The horizontal base extends base_length (60 mm) along X and is thickness (5 mm) tall
- A vertical upright rises from one end of the base to a total height of upright_height (50 mm) and is thickness (5 mm) wide

Pad the L-profile sketch by base_width (40 mm) along the Y axis.

**Step 3 — Link ALL dimensions to the Spreadsheet using expressions:**
Every constrained dimension in the sketch and the Pad length must be set via expressions referencing the Spreadsheet aliases (e.g., Spreadsheet.base_length). No hard-coded numeric values should remain for the four key dimensions.

**Step 4 — Modify a parameter to verify parametric linking:**
Open the Spreadsheet and change upright_height from 50 to 70 mm. The 3D model should recompute automatically, producing a taller bracket.

**Step 5 — Save:**
Save the document as: ~/Documents/FreeCAD/parametric_bracket.FCStd
